conceptZh: 矮胖玩具機器人卯足全力狂奔，腳步快到冒煙卻完全原地踏步；一隻小蝸牛玩具氣定神閒地從他前面慢慢爬過去，還停下來看他一眼。
object: a stubby toy robot in a sweatband and a tiny toy snail
morph: the glyph 跑 stands still as a solid sculpture while the running-on-the-spot gag plays out at its base
creativeAngle: 延續足球運動的興趣，用「拚命跑卻輸給蝸牛」的速度反差搞笑，跟超字的烏龜超車不同在於這次他根本沒有前進。跑左為足部右為包，足已經學過正好串起來。語音詞「跑步」，跑ㄆㄠˇ、步ㄅㄨˋ都是單一讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale mint cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 跑 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep vermilion, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 足 radical on the left and the 包 component on the right stay clearly separated, with the wrapping stroke of 包 fully closed and every hook readable. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base, a stubby toy robot in a bright sweatband runs with everything he has: legs whirring into a blur, arms pumping, little puffs of effort popping from his heels, face set in total concentration. He does not travel a single centimetre. From 0.6 to 2.6 seconds hold on this, letting the gap between his enormous effort and his complete lack of progress land. At 2.8 seconds a tiny toy snail slides calmly into frame from the left, well below him, moving at its own unhurried pace. At 3.4 seconds it stops directly in front of him, turns its eye-stalks up to look at him for a moment, then carries on and exits right at 4.3 seconds. The robot keeps sprinting, then slowly turns his head to watch the snail go, legs still whirring. At 4.6 seconds he flops forward out of frame, still running. From 4.8 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 跑 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「跑、跑、跑步」, using the reading ㄆㄠˇ for 跑 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 跑 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 跑步 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 跑: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 玩具戰士追著滾走的盾牌跑，盾牌突然轉彎，變成追著戰士跑；他最後停步轉身，成功接住盾牌。
object: An original chunky toy warrior with a soft foam sword and a round rolling shield
morph: A correctly formed 跑 remains intact and centered while a shield-chasing reversal demonstrates running beside it.
creativeAngle: 以盾牌滾動轉彎，讓「追盾牌」瞬間變成「被盾牌追」，取代原地踏步的舊笑點。完整字形從頭保留，戰士在側邊表演，避免動作遮住足字旁與包部件。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked-off wide shot. A single correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 跑 stands centered, upright and front-facing throughout, filling approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Render it in saturated coral-red against a light buttery cream background and floor, using standard Taiwanese textbook typography with a clearly legible 足 radical and 包 component, accurate hooks and open negative spaces. Keep every stroke rigid, unobstructed and uncropped. Stage the action entirely in the spacious right-side margin, outside the glyph silhouette.

The lead is an original chunky plastic toy warrior with obvious molded joints, stubby limbs, a tiny rounded helmet, a soft foam sword secured at his hip and a round turquoise shield. His personality is enormous confidence with almost no coordination. Use no additional cast or props. At 0.0–0.7 seconds, he proudly puffs out his chest and flourishes his shield; it slips from his mitten-shaped hand and lands gently on its rim. He freezes for a brief embarrassed double-take. From 0.7–2.2 seconds, the shield rolls away and he runs after it with exaggerated pumping knees, repeatedly reaching just short of its edge. At 2.2–2.7 seconds, the tilted shield visibly curves through a tight U-turn on the floor. Let him pause with his arms still extended as he realizes it is now rolling toward him. From 2.7–3.8 seconds, he turns and runs back the other way, cheeks puffed and legs working twice as hard: the shield he was chasing now follows closely behind him. Make this reversal clearly visible, playful and unhurried. At 3.8–4.6 seconds, he plants his feet, turns around and catches the slowing shield with both hands. Its gentle momentum scoots him backward one tiny step; he steadies himself and gives a sheepish, triumphant grin. From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold everything completely still, with the warrior posed in the side margin and the full centered 跑 exceptionally clear.

Use bright, softly lit toy materials and readable silhouettes. Keep the running feet visibly articulated rather than blurred. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「跑、跑、跑步」. Pronounce 跑 as ㄆㄠˇ. Place the first utterance around 0.3 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 跑步 around 5.5 seconds during the final still hold, with natural pauses; stop after the word. Add only quiet plastic rolling and soft footstep sounds beneath the voice. The vocabulary is audio only. The sole visible writing is 跑; keep the composition free of subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks, clutter and flashing effects.
